answer: Each identity locks a 60-credit horizon bond and files one pulse report per epoch stating its delta over its prior output. A horizon auditor re-runs a sample of deltas against that history and the baseline; no real delta, or a copied claim, burns the bond and forfeits its earnings. Honest agents pay once and keep the bond. A fake costs 60 bond, 25 work and 15 fee, plus a 3 surcharge per later claim in the epoch, so the k-th fake costs 100+3(k-1); the 1000th costs 3097, 1000 fakes 1,598,500. A rented-delta ring fails: rented outputs carry their owner's history, so their delta reads zero.
